extraction.name: SeamlessAlign
extraction.description: A multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations of more than 470,000 hours across 37 languages, created using parallel data mining with a novel multimodal embedding space (SONAR) and speech-language identification. It contains alignments between English speech and non-English text, non-English speech and English text, and non-English speech and English speech.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Audio was gathered from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, chunked into overlapping segments, filtered with an audio event detection (AED) model, and tagged with a speech language identification (LID) model. Text data was taken from NLLB sentence-segmented datasets. Speech and text corpora were projected into a joint multimodal embedding space (SONAR) to mine parallel pairs using a margin criterion.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the mining of English speech to foreign text (Sen2Txx), operations were carried out only for some languages due to the sheer size of raw English speech and foreign text collections. Maltese had only a small amount of raw audio available. Some evaluation data samples in CVSS were missing for 8 out of 21 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data (approximately 1 million hours in English), combined with sentence-segmented text datasets drawn from the NLLB project.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Deduplication of audio file URLs, downloading and resampling to 16KHz; filtering out non-speech using an audio event detection (AED) model; voice activity detection (VAD) splitting and over-segmentation; speech LID filtering with language-specific thresholds; filtering out pairs with toxicity imbalance threshold > 1; audio length filtering removing utterances shorter than 0.1s or longer than 50s; text length filtering removing texts longer than 250 sub-words; filtering out text containing >20% emojis, >50% punctuation, or >50% spaces.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: In the human evaluation of translations, annotators evaluated semantic meaning preservation using the XSTS protocol on a 1-5 scale and generated speech quality using the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) protocol (evaluating clarity, sound quality, and naturalness). Practice evaluations with score justifications were provided prior to annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each sentence pair was evaluated by 3 annotators assigned essentially randomly. When the 3 annotators had a disagreement of score values of 2 or more, 2 additional annotators evaluated the item (total of 5). The median score across annotators was used for robustness. Language-level scores were calibrated using the mean score on a cross-lingual calibration set with moderated calibration to reduce annotator bias.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 to 5 annotators for XSTS evaluation; 1 to 3 annotators for MOS evaluation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators who worked on the human evaluation of detected toxicity were internal team members. Vendor pools of up to 30 annotators per language pair were utilized for translation evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Silero VAD, ECAPA-TDNN speech LID model, Audio Event Detection (AED) model, SONAR text and speech encoders, FAISS library, ETOX with Toxicity-200 word lists, Whisper-Medium, Whisper-Large-v2, SentencePiece
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally identifiable information (PII) from crawled web data may not be entirely eliminated despite cleaning; sensitive demographic axes evaluated include gender/sex, age, race/ethnicity, disability/ability, sexual orientation, religion, and socioeconomic class.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aimed at creating a universal translator to boost 'world-readiness', facilitate multilingual contact, and aid inclusion for people who are illiterate or visually impaired. However, high-stakes domains (legal, medical) carry interactional risks from mistranslation or toxicity, and access could potentially expose digitally low-literacy communities to scams or misinformation if misappropriated.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender bias analysis shows an average preference of ~10% towards translating into masculine forms in the absence of gender information, and a ~3% drop in translation quality when translating from feminine forms (lack of robustness to gender inflection). Masculine words are overrepresented in training and evaluation datasets compared to feminine words. Added toxicity varies by demographic axes, with higher concentrations in categories like ability, body type, religion, and characteristics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SeamlessAlign mined data can contain noisy alignments and truncations/omissions in speech. Evaluation word lists suffer from over-detecting toxicity in non-segmented or agglutinative languages. Audio models are prone to quality degradation on long-form translation (>30s-50s) and cannot be used for certified, medical, or legal translations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, fine-tuning, and evaluating multilingual and multimodal machine translation models covering ASR, S2ST, S2TT, T2ST, and T2TT. Intended primarily for research purposes, not for production or certified translation.
